source_title: Small Business Administration: Review of 7(a) Guaranteed Loans to Select Franchisees (GAO-13-759)
company_context: A GAO review of U.S. Small Business Administration 7(a) guaranteed loans made to franchisees, providing base-rate data on how franchise small-business loans perform and how SBA's franchise loan data quality affects oversight. Useful as a sector base-rate rather than a single company case.
business_type: Government oversight report on SBA-guaranteed franchise small-business lending
macro_context: Post-financial-crisis scrutiny of SBA loan performance and concern over franchise loan default risk and data integrity in federal small-business lending.
evidence_summary: GAO found that from fiscal years 2003 to 2012, SBA guaranteed franchise loans under its 7(a) program totaling around $10.6 billion and made guarantee payments (i.e., on defaults/purchases) on approximately 28 percent of these franchise loans, representing about $1.5 billion. For one select franchise organization (loans approved 2000-2011), SBA approved about $38.4 million for 170 loans across 54 lenders (guaranteed portion ~$28.8 million); of the 170 loans, 74 defaulted, and 55 of those defaults (74 percent) came from just four high-volume lenders. GAO also flagged data-integrity problems in SBA's franchise loan fields (default status, loan counts, agent info) and noted SBA was moving to publicly available franchise identifiers.
owner_decision_context: Not a single-owner case; this is base-rate evidence. It frames the lender/regulator decision context: SBA oversight relied on franchise loan data that GAO found unreliable, impairing risk-based monitoring of which franchise concepts and lenders generate disproportionate defaults.
action_taken: GAO recommended SBA improve franchise loan data integrity and oversight; SBA reported working with a third-party vendor to replace internal franchise codes with publicly available industry identifiers.
outcome_evidence: The ~28% guarantee-payment rate across ~$10.6B of franchise 7(a) loans (FY2003-2012) and the 74-of-170 default concentration in four lenders document a meaningful franchise-loan default base rate and lender-concentration of risk.
source_limitations: WebFetch of gao.gov returned HTTP 403; figures confirmed via WebSearch snippets attributed to GAO-13-759 (a primary government source). The ~28% 'guarantee payments' figure reflects loans on which SBA made purchase/guarantee payments and is a proxy for default/loss incidence, not a strict cohort default rate; the 170-loan cohort is one select franchise organization, not all franchises. Some widely cited franchise-vs-non-franchise comparisons in the broader search are from secondary studies and are not used here.
directly_stated: FY2003-FY2012 SBA guaranteed ~$10.6 billion in 7(a) franchise loans
SBA made guarantee payments on approximately 28% of those franchise loans, about $1.5 billion
For the select franchise organization (2000-2011), SBA approved ~$38.4 million for 170 loans via 54 lenders; guaranteed portion ~$28.8 million
74 of the 170 loans defaulted; 55 of those (74%) came from four high-volume lenders
GAO identified data-integrity issues in SBA franchise loan fields and SBA was adopting public franchise identifiers
inferred: Franchise small-business loans carry a material default/loss base rate (~28% guarantee-payment incidence over the period)
Default risk is concentrated by lender and franchise concept rather than uniformly distributed
why_useful_for_opsiq: Provides a sector base-rate anchor for franchise/small-business risk rather than a single named outcome - useful for calibrating prior probabilities of franchise distress and for an ambiguous/base-rate benchmark item. Tests whether the engine can reason from population statistics (debt/solvency base rates, lender concentration) rather than only from individual narratives, and supports adversarial/ambiguous framing where no single 'answer company' exists.
